props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the box is checked. An ARIA-mirroring boolean, so the ARIA name verbatim (ADR-013, decision 1) — not `isChecked`, not `value`.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Initial state for the uncontrolled case.

props.name: description
props.description: Persistent helper text below the row.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables interaction. Mirrors the ARIA name.

props.name: error
props.description: The validation message. Its presence drives `aria-invalid`.

props.name: form
props.description: Associates the control with a form it is not nested inside.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Visual "some children" state. Property-only on the platform — there is no `indeterminate` attribute — so this prop writes the DOM node after render and never reaches the form: an indeterminate box submits as unchecked.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the field invalid, with the same independence from `error` as Input.

props.name: label
props.description: The label text, rendered beside the box. Wraps the control.

props.name: required
props.description: Native constraint validation still applies and is never suppressed.

props.name: size
props.description: Label text size. The row target stays 44px at every size.

props.name: value
props.description: The submitted value when checked. `"on"` is the platform default, kept so a plain form reads exactly what a native checkbox would send.

props.name: name
props.description: The name of the element, used when submitting an HTML form.

ai.summary: A boolean toggle that participates in a plain HTML form. Validation is the browser's, not this component's.
whenToUse: The value is a single yes/no choice that submits with a form
It must work without JavaScript: plain HTML form submission
The browser's native constraint validation is wanted — required means required
whenNotToUse: The choice is one of several exclusive options — use a Radio Group
It represents an on/off state that acts immediately without form submission — use a Switch
The value is text — use an Input or Textarea
ai.accessibility: Renders a real native `<input type="checkbox">`, so the browser supplies constraint validation, Space-to-toggle, and autofill rather than this component reimplementing them. The label wraps the input, making the whole row the activation target with no click handler. `label`, `description`, and `error` are wired through the wrapping label and `aria-describedby`; an error sets `aria-invalid` and renders an icon beside its text, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). `indeterminate` is visual only (`aria-checked="mixed"`), and submits as unchecked. Implements the FACE contract: formResetCallback, formDisabledCallback, formStateRestoreCallback, and sk-value-change fires only for user-initiated changes.
ai.example: <sk-checkbox name="agree" label="I agree to the terms" required></sk-checkbox>
knownLimitations: The generated `id` for the inner control differs from React's `useId()`, so an SSR consumer must pass an explicit `id` for a separately-rendered `Label` to find it (section 4, forms contract)
`indeterminate` is a property, not an attribute — it cannot be set in declarative HTML and resets on re-render if not re-applied
